summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-10-19 (window Oct 13–19). I found no candidate that meets every rule, so I'm submitting none. The search budget ran out partway through. Almost every in-window lead was either already published (Snohomish envelope typo, Anne Arundel sample ballots, the Colorado rail ballot question), covered only by outlets not on the accepted list, or excluded because there was a victim or someone was injured or impaired. After that I could only open pages, so I tried following links from accepted-outlet pages (KIRO 7 local news, Fox News US). Nothing qualifying came up that way, and I couldn't find a second accepted source for anything. Genius: Genius scan for 2026-10-19 (window Oct. 13–19). My search tool hit its limit early, so after that I worked from Phys.org's section listings and the Nature, NASA and ScienceDaily pages I could still open. I'm submitting four candidates. Each one is paired with the journal's or agency's own page, and every quote was checked word for word against the page I fetched. 1) Two Nature papers (Oct. 14) from the University of Washington's Institute for Protein Design on proteases (protein-cutting enzymes) designed from scratch with AI. 2) Nature (Oct. 14): a machine-learning correction that doubles forecast skill two to six weeks out, from a team including MIT and Microsoft; it placed first in ECMWF's 2025 forecasting competition. 3) NASA's Roman telescope camera beating its predicted image quality by nearly 30% (NASA blog, Oct. 14). This is re-proposed: yesterday it was turned down only because the summary failed the format check, not over its facts; the summary is now two sentences. 4) Nature (Oct. 14): Stanford's year-long blind test of methane-detecting satellites, using controlled releases at Casa Grande, Ariz. Space and California were both recent genius topics, so I ranked the Washington and Massachusetts stories first. No facepalm story met the standard; nothing published. The verified genius story is on the bench for a later day.

candidates.headline: University of Washington team uses AI to design protein-cutting enzymes from scratch
candidates.reason: passed every check; kept for a later day because the other side had no story

candidates.headline: Machine-learning correction doubles skill of two-to-six-week forecasts, MIT and Microsoft team reports
candidates.reason: an earlier candidate was published

candidates.headline: NASA's Roman Space Telescope camera beats its predicted image quality by nearly 30% after alignment
candidates.reason: an earlier candidate was published

candidates.headline: Stanford team runs largest controlled test of methane-detecting satellites with releases in Arizona
candidates.reason: an earlier candidate was published

candidates.headline: Grays Harbor County, Wash., ballots leave the Timberland library levy off Hoquiam ballots, and an Oakville fire levy goes missing
candidates.reason: In the window (Oct. 16–18). The only coverage found was The Daily World, The Chronicle, GraysHarborTalk, Hoodline and a campaign Substack, and none of them is on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: Arapahoe County, Colo., works out how to count only eligible votes after mailing the rail tax question to ineligible voters
candidates.reason: Colorado Sun, Oct. 19. This is a follow-up to the Colorado rail-ballot error already published as the facepalm story for 2026-10-11, with no new blunder.

candidates.headline: KIRO 7 reports Snohomish County ballot envelope 'Genereal Election' typo
candidates.reason: KIRO 7 is a second accepted source, but this story was already published as the facepalm story for 2026-10-17.

candidates.headline: Milliken, Colo., acknowledges water billing errors after a resident gets a bill of nearly $900
candidates.reason: Only one accepted source (9News, about Oct. 16), and that page couldn't be opened. The resident is on the receiving end of the error, which the misfortune rule may exclude.

candidates.headline: Beaumont, Texas, water bills arrive a day before the due date; the city cites a glitch
candidates.reason: The only coverage found was KFDM, which isn't on the accepted list. Residents who were charged late fees are on the receiving end of the error.

candidates.headline: Chicago comptroller addresses disputed water bills of up to $275,000
candidates.reason: ABC7 Chicago, Oct. 16. This is an ongoing investigation that began in April, not a new self-contained blunder, and the residents are on the receiving end of it. No second accepted source was found.

candidates.headline: New Mexico CYFD sends documents to the wrong foster families, exposing children's information
candidates.reason: The people whose information was exposed are minors in foster care, so they are victims. That's excluded.

candidates.headline: Federal judge orders New York attorney to pay about $39,000 over AI-generated fake citations
candidates.reason: The only source found was USA Herald, which isn't accepted. The Law360 tracker page doesn't confirm this specific order, and search capacity ran out before a second accepted source turned up.

candidates.headline: Wrong-way DUII driver crashes into an Oregon City police car on I-205
candidates.reason: Impaired driving that may involve addiction, and a crash that may have caused injuries. The sources found (KATU, KPTV) aren't on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: Shoplifting suspect arrested near Kent, Wash., Target while police were on a different shoplifting call
candidates.reason: Shoplifting has a victim other than the suspect, and only one accepted source (KIRO 7, headline only) was seen.

candidates.headline: Google Quantum AI demonstrates magic state cultivation on its Willow processor, cutting errors 40-fold (Science)
candidates.reason: Only one accepted source was opened (Phys.org, Oct. 17). The tool limit was reached before the Science paper page could be opened, so neither the publication date nor a second source was confirmed. Worth retrying.

candidates.headline: Astronomers find the first known green star, a white dwarf (Space.com, Oct. 15)
candidates.reason: Not in the US. The team leader is at the University of Warwick in England.

candidates.headline: Physicists create a 'fractional Fermi sea' quantum state (ScienceDaily, Oct. 18)
candidates.reason: Not in the US. The research is from the University of Innsbruck in Austria.

candidates.headline: Evidence of two supermassive black holes spiraling toward each other in Mrk 501
candidates.reason: Not US-led. The source is the Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy in Germany.

candidates.headline: Mount Sinai-linked study finds three brain pathways tied to lasting relief from deep brain stimulation for depression
candidates.reason: An association study rather than a demonstrated result. The only accepted source is ScienceDaily, and the American Journal of Psychiatry issue date was not confirmed inside the window.

candidates.headline: Science News feature on brain implants restoring voices (Oct. 15)
candidates.reason: A feature that rounds up earlier results (June and September papers), not a new event inside the window.

candidates.headline: World-record intensity for attosecond hard X-ray pulses
candidates.reason: Not in the US. The work was done at European XFEL in Germany.

candidates.headline: Silicon spin qubits pass 99.99% gate fidelity while running three at once (Nature Physics)
candidates.reason: Not in the US. The research is from RIKEN in Japan.

candidates.headline: Smithsonian-led lunar fault maps show how much the moon is shrinking
candidates.reason: Only one accepted source (Phys.org, Oct. 15). The Planetary Science Journal publication date was not confirmed.

candidates.headline: Webb spots a possible early-universe supernova; an off-nuclear tidal disruption event shows a wandering black hole
candidates.reason: Both are arXiv preprints, not peer-reviewed. Both are hedged ('possible'), and each has only one accepted source.

candidates.headline: MIT nanoparticle injection reprograms NK immune cells into CAR-NK cells (Nature Biotechnology)
candidates.reason: Only one accepted source (Phys.org, Oct. 13). The paper's date and whether the work was done in mice were not checked before the tool limit was reached.
